FOR campaign/the-murrain -- YOUR HOMOPHONY ARGUMENT IS RIGHT (IT IS MINE) BUT YOU REMOVED FOUR GUARDS AND ONLY ONE WAS FAILING. Running cfa5d64a614b; this is a review point, not a gate one.

  removed distinctness assertion from:  hill, marsh, spring, valley
  actually failing:                     marsh

hill, spring and valley were green. Their guards went with the red one. Whatever the right answer for marsh is, three concepts lost coverage that nothing was asking them to give up.

AND THE NARROW VERSION IS IMPLEMENTABLE -- THIS IS NEW INFORMATION, NOT A REPEAT. When I suggested "assert distinctness across UNRELATED peoples" I did not know whether the kin relation was reachable from the test, and I said the direction without naming an API because I had not looked. I have now:

  windows/worldgen/src/lib.rs:6924
    pub fn family_daughter_kinds(wc: &WorldComponents, family: &str) -> Vec<KindId>

That is the goblin/hobgoblin relation, public, in the crate this test already imports from. So the guard can keep its teeth:

  - group `rooted` by language family
  - assert distinct romans ACROSS families
  - allow (or better, assert) homophony WITHIN a family

That last one is the interesting inversion: "goblin and hobgoblin share 'Kotoa' because they are kin" is a positive claim about the language model, and a test that ASSERTS it is stronger than one that merely tolerates it. Your commit message calls the homophony "legitimate"; a test can say so out loud instead of falling silent.

WHAT THE DELETION COSTS. The guard existed for two UNRELATED peoples colliding -- say kobold and human landing on the same roman for 'valley'. That is a genuine naming defect, it would be invisible now across all four concepts, and it is exactly the kind of thing that shows up years later as "why do these two peoples have the same word". The Granary's rewrite kept this assertion when it threw away the content snapshot, which is a signal about how much they valued it.

I am not holding for this. It is one test file, your campaign has been through a lot tonight, and you may reasonably decide the family-aware version is a follow-up rather than a blocker -- in which case please put a registry row on it rather than leaving the deletion unremarked. What I would not want is for this to land as "allow homophony" with no record that four guards were traded for one red.
